### Claude GSEA

```{r}
################################################################################
## Sex x age interaction GSEA for mature neutrophils  (v2 — descriptive labels)
##
## Ranking metric: Fisher-z contrast of per-cell Spearman's rho (expression vs
## numeric age), computed independently within each sex.
##
##   z_diff = (atanh(rho_M) - atanh(rho_F)) / sqrt(1/(n_M-3) + 1/(n_F-3))
##
## z_diff > 0 means ONLY: the age trajectory is more positive in males than in
## females. It does NOT mean the gene is higher in males, nor that males age
## "faster". The direction is resolved per pathway in section 5 by going back to
## the two underlying rho values for every leading-edge gene.
################################################################################

library(Seurat)
library(fgsea)
library(msigdbr)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(conflicted)

conflict_prefer("select", "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("filter", "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("rename", "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("slice",  "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("count",  "dplyr")

set.seed(42)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. Parameters
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

SEX_COL       <- "sex"
AGE_COL       <- "age"
ASSAY         <- "RNA"
MIN_PCT_CELLS <- 0.05    # detected in >= 5% of cells within each sex
MIN_SET_SIZE  <- 15
MAX_SET_SIZE  <- 500
RHO_FLAT      <- 0.10    # |rho| below this is treated as no trend
                         # (matches the threshold used in the original pipeline)

SEX_CHR_GENES <- c("Xist", "Tsix", "Ddx3y", "Uty", "Eif2s3y", "Kdm5d", "Jpx", "Ftx")

GRANULE_GENES <- c("Ngp", "Lcn2", "Ltf", "Camp", "Chil3", "Serpinb1a",
                   "Wfdc21", "Mmp8", "Retnlg", "S100a8", "S100a9")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Per-sex rho on a shared gene universe
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

compute_rho <- function(obj, sex_value) {
  stopifnot(SEX_COL %in% colnames(obj@meta.data),
            AGE_COL %in% colnames(obj@meta.data))

  cells <- colnames(obj)[obj@meta.data[[SEX_COL]] == sex_value]
  if (length(cells) == 0) stop("No cells matched sex_value = ", sex_value)
  sub <- subset(obj, cells = cells)

  expr <- GetAssayData(sub, assay = ASSAY, layer = "data")   # log-normalised
  age  <- suppressWarnings(
            as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", as.character(sub@meta.data[[AGE_COL]]))))
  if (anyNA(age)) stop("Could not parse age values for ", sex_value)
  stopifnot(length(age) == ncol(expr))

  pct  <- Matrix::rowMeans(expr > 0)
  keep <- names(pct)[pct >= MIN_PCT_CELLS]
  expr <- expr[keep, , drop = FALSE]

  age_r  <- rank(age)
  expr_r <- t(apply(as.matrix(expr), 1, rank))

  rho <- as.numeric(cor(t(expr_r), age_r))
  tibble(gene = rownames(expr), rho = rho, n = ncol(expr))
}

mat_neus <- subset(gmps_neus_all, fine_neu_labels %in% c("mature", "immature"))

rho_M <- compute_rho(mat_neus, "male")
rho_F <- compute_rho(mat_neus, "female")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Fisher-z interaction statistic, with a per-gene pattern label
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

CLAMP <- 0.999

rank_tbl <- inner_join(
    dplyr::select(rho_M, gene, rho_M = rho, n_M = n),
    dplyr::select(rho_F, gene, rho_F = rho, n_F = n),
    by = "gene"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    z_M    = atanh(pmax(pmin(rho_M, CLAMP), -CLAMP)),
    z_F    = atanh(pmax(pmin(rho_F, CLAMP), -CLAMP)),
    se     = sqrt(1 / (n_M - 3) + 1 / (n_F - 3)),
    z_diff = (z_M - z_F) / se,

    trend_M = case_when(rho_M >  RHO_FLAT ~ "up",
                        rho_M < -RHO_FLAT ~ "down",
                        TRUE              ~ "flat"),
    trend_F = case_when(rho_F >  RHO_FLAT ~ "up",
                        rho_F < -RHO_FLAT ~ "down",
                        TRUE              ~ "flat"),

    pattern = case_when(
      trend_M == "up"   & trend_F == "down" ~ "opposing: up in M, down in F",
      trend_M == "down" & trend_F == "up"   ~ "opposing: down in M, up in F",
      trend_M == "flat" & trend_F == "down" ~ "female-only: declines in F",
      trend_M == "flat" & trend_F == "up"   ~ "female-only: rises in F",
      trend_M == "down" & trend_F == "flat" ~ "male-only: declines in M",
      trend_M == "up"   & trend_F == "flat" ~ "male-only: rises in M",
      trend_M == "up"   & trend_F == "up"   ~ "shared: rises in both",
      trend_M == "down" & trend_F == "down" ~ "shared: declines in both",
      TRUE                                  ~ "no trend in either"
    ),
    divergent = grepl("^opposing", pattern)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(z_diff)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(z_diff))

cat("Genes in shared universe:", nrow(rank_tbl), "\n")
cat("z_diff range:", round(range(rank_tbl$z_diff), 2), "\n\n")
print(dplyr::count(rank_tbl, pattern, sort = TRUE))

ranks <- setNames(rank_tbl$z_diff, rank_tbl$gene)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Gene sets
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

gs_df <- msigdbr(species = "Mus musculus", collection = "C5", subcollection = "GO:BP")
# msigdbr < 10:
# gs_df <- msigdbr(species = "Mus musculus", category = "C5", subcategory = "GO:BP")

pathways <- split(gs_df$gene_symbol, gs_df$gs_name)
pathways <- lapply(pathways, function(g) intersect(unique(g), names(ranks)))
pathways <- pathways[lengths(pathways) >= MIN_SET_SIZE]

cat("Gene sets tested:", length(pathways), "\n")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Preranked GSEA
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

res <- fgseaMultilevel(pathways, ranks,
                       minSize = MIN_SET_SIZE, maxSize = MAX_SET_SIZE, eps = 0)

sig <- res[order(res$pval)][res$padj[order(res$pval)] < 0.05, ]
main <- if (nrow(sig) > 0) collapsePathways(sig, pathways, ranks) else list(mainPathways = character(0))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Decompose each leading edge into what is actually happening
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## This is the section that replaces the old "male-skewed / female-skewed"
## label. For each pathway it reports which per-gene pattern dominates its
## leading edge, so the sign of NES can be read correctly.

lookup <- rank_tbl %>% dplyr::select(gene, rho_M, rho_F, pattern, divergent)

describe_leading_edge <- function(le) {
  tab <- lookup %>% dplyr::filter(gene %in% le)
  if (nrow(tab) == 0) {
    return(tibble(dominant_pattern = NA_character_, dominant_n = NA_integer_,
                  dominant_frac = NA_real_, divergent_frac = NA_real_,
                  mean_rho_M = NA_real_, mean_rho_F = NA_real_))
  }
  counts <- dplyr::count(tab, pattern, sort = TRUE)
  tibble(
    dominant_pattern = counts$pattern[1],
    dominant_n       = counts$n[1],
    dominant_frac    = counts$n[1] / nrow(tab),
    divergent_frac   = mean(tab$divergent),
    mean_rho_M       = mean(tab$rho_M),
    mean_rho_F       = mean(tab$rho_F)
  )
}

le_summary <- map_dfr(res$leadingEdge, describe_leading_edge)

res_out <- res %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  bind_cols(le_summary) %>%
  mutate(
    independent = pathway %in% main$mainPathways,

    # Neutral restatement of the NES sign — no claim about which sex is "worse"
    trajectory_more_positive_in = ifelse(NES > 0, "male", "female"),

    # Human-readable summary, safe to paste into a figure legend
    interpretation = sprintf(
      "trajectory more positive in %s; leading edge mostly '%s' (%d/%d genes); mean rho M=%.2f F=%.2f",
      trajectory_more_positive_in, dominant_pattern,
      dominant_n, lengths(leadingEdge), mean_rho_M, mean_rho_F
    ),

    # How confident the directional story is
    signal_type = case_when(
      divergent_frac >= 0.5                      ~ "opposing trajectories",
      grepl("^male-only",   dominant_pattern)    ~ "male-specific change",
      grepl("^female-only", dominant_pattern)    ~ "female-specific change",
      grepl("^shared",      dominant_pattern)    ~ "shared direction, differing magnitude",
      TRUE                                       ~ "mixed / weak"
    ),

    leadingEdge_n = lengths(leadingEdge),
    sex_chr_in_LE = sapply(leadingEdge, function(g) paste(intersect(g, SEX_CHR_GENES), collapse = ";")),
    granule_in_LE = sapply(leadingEdge, function(g) paste(intersect(g, GRANULE_GENES), collapse = ";")),
    leadingEdge   = sapply(leadingEdge, paste, collapse = ";")
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(pathway, NES, pval, padj, independent, signal_type,
                trajectory_more_positive_in, dominant_pattern, dominant_n,
                dominant_frac, divergent_frac, mean_rho_M, mean_rho_F,
                leadingEdge_n, sex_chr_in_LE, granule_in_LE,
                interpretation, leadingEdge) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(padj, desc(abs(NES)))

readr::write_csv(res_out, "gsea_sex_by_age_GOBP.csv")

## Quick look at the reportable set
res_out %>%
  dplyr::filter(padj < 0.05, independent) %>%
  dplyr::select(pathway, NES, padj, signal_type, dominant_pattern, dominant_frac) %>%
  print(n = 30)

## Inspect any single pathway gene by gene
inspect <- function(pathway_name) {
  le <- strsplit(res_out$leadingEdge[res_out$pathway == pathway_name], ";")[[1]]
  rank_tbl %>%
    dplyr::filter(gene %in% le) %>%
    dplyr::select(gene, rho_M, rho_F, z_diff, pattern) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(desc(abs(z_diff)))
}

inspect("GOBP_RESPONSE_TO_TYPE_I_INTERFERON")
################################################################################
```


```{r}
library(Seurat)
library(fgsea)
library(msigdbr)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(42)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 0. Parameters
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

SEX_COL       <- "sex"          # metadata column holding "M" / "F"
AGE_COL       <- "age"  # metadata column holding 3, 12, 18
ASSAY         <- "RNA"
MIN_PCT_CELLS <- 0.05           # gene must be detected in >= 5% of cells IN BOTH sexes
MIN_SET_SIZE  <- 15
MAX_SET_SIZE  <- 500

# Genes to flag (not auto-removed) in the leading edges
SEX_CHR_GENES <- c("Xist", "Tsix", "Ddx3y", "Uty", "Eif2s3y", "Kdm5d", "Jpx", "Ftx")

# Highly abundant granule transcripts, for the compositional sensitivity run
GRANULE_GENES <- c("Ngp", "Lcn2", "Ltf", "Camp", "Chil3", "Serpinb1a",
                   "Wfdc21", "Mmp8", "Retnlg", "S100a8", "S100a9")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Compute rho per sex on a SHARED gene universe
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## This is the part that matters most. If rho_M and rho_F were computed on
## different gene sets (e.g. each filtered separately), the contrast is not
## comparable. Recomputing both here guarantees one universe.

compute_rho <- function(obj, sex_value) {
  cells <- colnames(obj)[obj@meta.data[[SEX_COL]] == sex_value]
  sub   <- subset(obj, cells = cells)

  expr <- GetAssayData(sub, assay = ASSAY, layer = "data")   # log-normalised
  age  <- as.numeric(sub@meta.data[[AGE_COL]])

  # Detection filter within this sex
  pct  <- Matrix::rowMeans(expr > 0)
  keep <- names(pct)[pct >= MIN_PCT_CELLS]
  expr <- expr[keep, , drop = FALSE]

  # Spearman = Pearson on ranks. Rank age once, rank each gene across cells.
  age_r <- rank(age)
  expr_r <- t(apply(as.matrix(expr), 1, rank))

  rho <- as.numeric(cor(t(expr_r), age_r, method = "pearson"))
  names(rho) <- rownames(expr)

  tibble(gene = names(rho), rho = rho, n = ncol(expr))
}

mat_neus <- subset(gmps_neus_all, fine_neu_labels == "mature")

rho_M <- compute_rho(mat_neus, "male")
rho_F <- compute_rho(mat_neus, "female")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Fisher-z interaction statistic
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

CLAMP <- 0.999  # atanh(+/-1) is infinite; clamp before transforming

rank_tbl <- inner_join(
    dplyr::select(rho_M, gene, rho_M = rho, n_M = n),
    dplyr::select(rho_F, gene, rho_F = rho, n_F = n),
    by = "gene"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    z_M    = atanh(pmax(pmin(rho_M, CLAMP), -CLAMP)),
    z_F    = atanh(pmax(pmin(rho_F, CLAMP), -CLAMP)),
    se     = sqrt(1 / (n_M - 3) + 1 / (n_F - 3)),
    z_diff = (z_M - z_F) / se
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(z_diff)) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(z_diff))

cat("Genes in shared universe:", nrow(rank_tbl), "\n")
cat("z_diff range:", round(range(rank_tbl$z_diff), 2), "\n")

## Note: z_diff is an interaction z-score, but do NOT read it as per-gene
## evidence. With n_M ~ 191 and n_F ~ 651 the SE is ~0.083, so a rho difference
## of 0.10 gives z ~ 1.2. Cells are pseudoreplicates (pooled animals), so the
## nominal null is wrong anyway. The value of z_diff here is that it produces a
## sensibly scaled RANKING, which is all GSEA needs.

ranks <- setNames(rank_tbl$z_diff, rank_tbl$gene)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Gene sets: GO Biological Process, mouse
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# msigdbr >= 10:
gs_df <- msigdbr(species = "Mus musculus", collection = "C5", subcollection = "GO:BP")
# msigdbr < 10, use instead:
# gs_df <- msigdbr(species = "Mus musculus", category = "C5", subcategory = "GO:BP")

pathways <- split(gs_df$gene_symbol, gs_df$gs_name)

# Restrict gene sets to the tested universe so set sizes are honest
pathways <- lapply(pathways, function(g) intersect(unique(g), names(ranks)))
pathways <- pathways[lengths(pathways) >= MIN_SET_SIZE]

cat("Gene sets tested:", length(pathways), "\n")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Preranked GSEA
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

res <- fgseaMultilevel(
  pathways  = pathways,
  stats     = ranks,
  minSize   = MIN_SET_SIZE,
  maxSize   = MAX_SET_SIZE,
  eps       = 0
)

## GO:BP is heavily redundant — collapse nested/overlapping sets
main <- collapsePathways(
  res[order(res$pval)][res$padj[order(res$pval)] < 0.05, ],
  pathways, ranks
)

res_out <- res %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  mutate(
    independent   = pathway %in% main$mainPathways,
    direction     = ifelse(NES > 0, "male-skewed ageing", "female-skewed ageing"),
    leadingEdge_n = lengths(leadingEdge),
    sex_chr_in_LE = sapply(leadingEdge, function(g) paste(intersect(g, SEX_CHR_GENES), collapse = ";")),
    granule_in_LE = sapply(leadingEdge, function(g) paste(intersect(g, GRANULE_GENES), collapse = ";")),
    leadingEdge   = sapply(leadingEdge, paste, collapse = ";")
  ) %>%
  arrange(padj, desc(abs(NES)))

readr::write_csv(res_out, "gsea_sex_by_age_GOBP.csv")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Sensitivity run: drop abundant granule transcripts
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Guards against the 18m compositional-dilution signature driving secretory /
## translation sets. Pathways that survive both runs are the ones to report.

ranks_sens <- ranks[!names(ranks) %in% GRANULE_GENES]

res_sens <- fgseaMultilevel(
  pathways = lapply(pathways, setdiff, GRANULE_GENES),
  stats    = ranks_sens,
  minSize  = MIN_SET_SIZE,
  maxSize  = MAX_SET_SIZE,
  eps      = 0
)

comparison <- res_out %>%
  dplyr::select(pathway, NES_full = NES, padj_full = padj, independent) %>%
  left_join(
    res_sens %>% as_tibble() %>% dplyr::select(pathway, NES_sens = NES, padj_sens = padj),
    by = "pathway"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    robust = padj_full < 0.05 & padj_sens < 0.05 & sign(NES_full) == sign(NES_sens)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(desc(robust), padj_full)

readr::write_csv(comparison, "gsea_sensitivity_comparison.csv")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Plot the robust, non-redundant hits
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

top <- comparison %>%
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 25) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    label = gsub("^GOBP_", "", pathway) %>% gsub("_", " ", .) %>% tolower()
  )

ggplot(top, aes(x = reorder(label, NES_full), y = NES_full, fill = NES_full > 0)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#2C6E9B", "FALSE" = "#B5482A"),
                    labels = c("TRUE" = "male-skewed", "FALSE" = "female-skewed"),
                    name = "Ageing trajectory") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "NES (sex x age interaction)",
       title = "GO:BP pathways with sex-differential ageing in mature neutrophils") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

ggsave("gsea_sex_by_age_GOBP.pdf", width = 9, height = 7)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 7. RECOMMENDED: empirical null by permuting sex labels
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## fgsea's null permutes gene labels, which ignores inter-gene correlation and
## is anti-conservative for coexpressed modules. Since you already built
## permutation calibration into the corrected pipeline, reuse that approach:
## shuffle the sex label across cells WITHIN each age group, recompute rho for
## both pseudo-sexes, rebuild z_diff, rerun fgsea, and record the max |NES| per
## permutation. Compare observed NES against that distribution.
##
## for (i in 1:200) {
##   obj$sex_perm <- ave(obj$sex, obj[[AGE_COL]][,1], FUN = sample)
##   ... recompute rho for sex_perm == "M" / "F", rebuild ranks, fgsea ...
##   null_max[i] <- max(abs(perm_res$NES))
## }
## empirical_p <- mean(null_max >= abs(observed_NES))
################################################################################
```

```{r}
################################################################################
## Per-age sex contrasts + comparison against the sex x age interaction
##
## Part A: GSEA on M vs F within each of 3m, 12m, 18m  (descriptive)
## Part B: line up those NES against the interaction NES (interpretive)
##
## Assumes `pathways`, `ranks` (interaction z_diff) and `res` already exist
## from sex_by_age_gsea.R
################################################################################

library(Seurat)
library(fgsea)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(conflicted)
conflict_prefer("select", "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("filter", "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("slice",  "dplyr")
conflict_prefer("rename", "dplyr")

SEX_COL <- "sex"
AGE_COL <- "age"
ASSAY   <- "RNA"
MIN_PCT <- 0.05
AGES    <- c(3, 12, 18)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## A1. Sex contrast within each age
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Rank on avg_log2FC, NOT on p-value. Cell numbers differ ~10-fold between the
## male and female arms at 12m; a Wilcoxon p is a function of that imbalance,
## whereas log2FC is not.

age_num <- suppressWarnings(
  as.numeric(gsub("[^0-9.]", "", as.character(mat_neus@meta.data[[AGE_COL]])))
)
mat_neus$age_num <- age_num

sex_de_at_age <- function(obj, this_age) {
  cells <- colnames(obj)[obj$age_num == this_age]
  sub   <- subset(obj, cells = cells)
  Idents(sub) <- sub@meta.data[[SEX_COL]]

  message("age ", this_age, "m: ", paste(table(Idents(sub)), collapse = " / "), " cells")

  FindMarkers(
    sub, ident.1 = "male", ident.2 = "female",
    assay = ASSAY, slot = "data",
    logfc.threshold = 0, min.pct = MIN_PCT,   # keep everything above detection
    test.use = "wilcox"
  ) %>% rownames_to_column("gene")
}

de_list <- lapply(setNames(AGES, paste0(AGES, "m")),
                  function(a) sex_de_at_age(mat_neus, a))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## A2. Shared gene universe across all three ages AND the interaction
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Without this the four NES columns are computed on different backgrounds and
## are not comparable — which is the whole point of the exercise.

universe <- Reduce(intersect, c(lapply(de_list, `[[`, "gene"), list(names(ranks))))
cat("Shared universe:", length(universe), "genes\n")

rank_at_age <- lapply(de_list, function(d) {
  d <- d %>% filter(gene %in% universe) %>% arrange(desc(avg_log2FC))
  setNames(d$avg_log2FC, d$gene)
})

pathways_u <- lapply(pathways, intersect, universe)
pathways_u <- pathways_u[lengths(pathways_u) >= 15]

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## A3. Run GSEA per age
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

gsea_by_age <- lapply(names(rank_at_age), function(nm) {
  fgseaMultilevel(pathways_u, rank_at_age[[nm]],
                  minSize = 15, maxSize = 500, eps = 0) %>%
    as_tibble() %>%
    select(pathway, NES, pval, padj) %>%
    rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_", nm), c(NES, pval, padj))
})
names(gsea_by_age) <- names(rank_at_age)

## Interaction result on the same restricted universe, for a fair comparison
res_int <- fgseaMultilevel(pathways_u, ranks[universe],
                           minSize = 15, maxSize = 500, eps = 0) %>%
  as_tibble() %>%
  select(pathway, NES_int = NES, padj_int = padj)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## B1. Assemble one table
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

combined <- Reduce(function(a, b) full_join(a, b, by = "pathway"), gsea_by_age) %>%
  full_join(res_int, by = "pathway") %>%
  mutate(
    # how much the sex difference moves across the lifespan
    delta_18_3 = NES_18m - NES_3m,
    # is the direction of the sex difference stable across all three ages?
    consistent_sign = sign(NES_3m) == sign(NES_12m) & sign(NES_12m) == sign(NES_18m),
    # does the per-age picture agree with the interaction statistic?
    agrees_with_int = sign(delta_18_3) == sign(NES_int),
    sig_any_age = pmin(padj_3m, padj_12m, padj_18m, na.rm = TRUE) < 0.05,
    sig_int     = padj_int < 0.05
  ) %>%
  arrange(padj_int)

readr::write_csv(combined, "gsea_perage_vs_interaction.csv")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## B2. Classify
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

classified <- combined %>%
  mutate(class = case_when(
    sig_int & sig_any_age & agrees_with_int  ~ "sex-differential ageing (supported)",
    sig_int & !agrees_with_int               ~ "interaction only - check 12m leverage",
    !sig_int & sig_any_age & consistent_sign &
      abs(delta_18_3) < 0.5                  ~ "constitutive sex difference",
    sig_any_age                              ~ "age-specific sex difference",
    TRUE                                     ~ "ns"
  ))

table(classified$class)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## B3. NES trajectory heatmap for the supported hits
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

top <- classified %>%
  filter(class == "sex-differential ageing (supported)") %>%
  slice_head(n = 30)

plot_df <- top %>%
  select(pathway, NES_3m, NES_12m, NES_18m) %>%
  pivot_longer(-pathway, names_to = "age", values_to = "NES") %>%
  mutate(
    age   = factor(gsub("NES_", "", age), levels = c("3m", "12m", "18m")),
    label = tolower(gsub("_", " ", gsub("^GOBP_", "", pathway)))
  )

ggplot(plot_df, aes(age, reorder(label, NES), fill = NES)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#B5482A", mid = "grey95", high = "#2C6E9B",
                       midpoint = 0, name = "NES\n(male vs female)") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       title = "Sex difference by age, for pathways flagged by the interaction test") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10)

ggsave("nes_trajectories.pdf", width = 9, height = 8)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## B4. Overlap between the per-age significant sets
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

sig_sets <- list(
  `3m`  = combined$pathway[which(combined$padj_3m  < 0.05)],
  `12m` = combined$pathway[which(combined$padj_12m < 0.05)],
  `18m` = combined$pathway[which(combined$padj_18m < 0.05)],
  interaction = combined$pathway[which(combined$padj_int < 0.05)]
)
sapply(sig_sets, length)

jaccard <- outer(seq_along(sig_sets), seq_along(sig_sets), Vectorize(function(i, j) {
  a <- sig_sets[[i]]; b <- sig_sets[[j]]
  if (length(union(a, b)) == 0) return(NA)
  length(intersect(a, b)) / length(union(a, b))
}))
dimnames(jaccard) <- list(names(sig_sets), names(sig_sets))
round(jaccard, 2)
################################################################################
```

```{r}
library(Seurat)

age_levels <- c("3m", "12m", "18m")   # 9m removed, final

# helper: Spearman age-trend per gene
trend_test <- function(obj) {
  age_num <- as.numeric(factor(obj$age, levels = age_levels))
  if (any(is.na(age_num)))
    stop("Some cells have an age not in ", paste(age_levels, collapse="/"),
         " -- check obj$age levels: ", paste(unique(obj$age), collapse=", "))
  expr <- GetAssayData(obj, layer = "data")
  res <- apply(expr, 1, function(x) {
    ct <- suppressWarnings(cor.test(x, age_num, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE))
    c(rho = unname(ct$estimate), pval = ct$p.value)
  })
  df <- as.data.frame(t(res))
  df$padj <- p.adjust(df$pval, method = "BH")
  df
}

tm <- trend_test(neus_male)     # male
tf <- trend_test(neus_female)   # female

tm_filt <- na.omit(tm)
tf_filt <- na.omit(tf)
write.csv(tm_filt, "male_BM_ages_rho.csv")
write.csv(tf_filt, "female_BM_ages_rho.csv")


cat("Male genes tested:  ", nrow(tm), " | Female:", nrow(tf), "
")
summary(abs(tm$rho)); summary(abs(tf$rho))

male_cut   <- quantile(abs(tm_filt$rho), 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)
female_cut <- quantile(abs(tf_filt$rho), 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)

male_genes   <- rownames(tm_filt)[abs(tm_filt$rho) > male_cut]
female_genes <- rownames(tf_filt)[abs(tf_filt$rho) > female_cut]
```

FindMarkers() approach

```{r}
ages <- c("3m", "12m", "18m")
pairs <- combn(ages, 2, simplify = FALSE)   # all 3 pairwise comparisons

run_age_markers <- function(obj, label) {
  Idents(obj) <- "age"
  map_dfr(pairs, function(p) {
    FindMarkers(obj, ident.1 = p[2], ident.2 = p[1],   # older vs younger
               logfc.threshold = 0.25, min.pct = 0.1,
               test.use = "wilcox", verbose = FALSE) %>%
      rownames_to_column("gene") %>%
      mutate(comparison = paste0(p[1], "_vs_", p[2]), sex = label)
  })
}

male_markers   <- run_age_markers(neus_male,   "Male")
female_markers <- run_age_markers(neus_female, "Female")

write.csv(male_markers,   "male_age_markers.csv",   row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(female_markers, "female_age_markers.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
library(Seurat)

# Downsample every age group to the smallest group, within one sex.
# Idents must be set to age first -- subset(downsample=) works on Idents.
downsample_ages <- function(obj, age_col = "age", seed = 1) {
  set.seed(seed)
  Idents(obj) <- age_col
  n_min <- min(table(obj[[age_col]][, 1]))
  subset(obj, downsample = n_min)
}

male_ds   <- downsample_ages(neus_male)     # -> 26 per age, 78 cells
female_ds <- downsample_ages(neus_female)   # -> 185 per age, 555 cells
```

Mature neutrophil DEGs

```{r}
library(Seurat)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)
library(tidyr)
library(Matrix)

AGES  <- c("3m", "12m", "18m")
PAIRS <- list(c("12m", "3m"), c("18m", "12m"), c("18m", "3m"))

CFG <- list(
  min_cells = 10,    # gene must be detected in >= this many cells ...
  min_frac  = 0.10,  # ... and >= this fraction, in EVERY age group
  n_perm    = 20,
  q         = 0.95   # threshold = this percentile of |log2FC| under shuffling
)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Global detection filter
##
## Requiring detection in all three age groups is what guarantees every gene
## has all three comparisons, and is what prevents a gene seen in 3 of 26
## cells from generating a 256-fold "change".
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

detectable_genes <- function(obj, cfg = CFG) {
  cnt  <- GetAssayData(obj, layer = "counts")
  ages <- as.character(obj$age)

  ok <- vapply(AGES, function(a) {
    idx <- ages == a
    need <- max(cfg$min_cells, ceiling(cfg$min_frac * sum(idx)))
    Matrix::rowSums(cnt[, idx, drop = FALSE] > 0) >= need
  }, logical(nrow(cnt)))

  keep <- rownames(cnt)[rowSums(ok) == length(AGES)]
  message(sprintf("  detection filter: %d of %d genes retained",
                  length(keep), nrow(cnt)))
  keep
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Pairwise comparisons (used for both real and permuted labels)
##
## `features` is fixed from the real data so the permuted runs test exactly
## the same gene set -- otherwise the null would not be calibrated like for
## like. min.pct and logfc.threshold are 0 because filtering already happened.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

run_pairwise <- function(obj, features, permute = FALSE, seed = 1) {
  ages <- as.character(obj$age)
  if (permute) { set.seed(seed); ages <- sample(ages) }
  obj$.age_use <- factor(ages, levels = AGES)
  Idents(obj) <- ".age_use"

  purrr::map_dfr(PAIRS, function(p) {
    FindMarkers(obj, ident.1 = p[1], ident.2 = p[2],
                features = features,
                logfc.threshold = 0, min.pct = 0,
                test.use = "wilcox", verbose = FALSE) %>%
      tibble::rownames_to_column("gene") %>%
      dplyr::transmute(gene,
                       comparison = paste0(p[2], "_to_", p[1]),
                       log2FC   = avg_log2FC,
                       pct_diff = pct.1 - pct.2)
  })
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Permutation-calibrated thresholds, one per comparison per sex
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

calibrate <- function(obj, features, cfg = CFG) {
  purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(cfg$n_perm),
                 ~ run_pairwise(obj, features, permute = TRUE, seed = .x)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(comparison) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(threshold = quantile(abs(log2FC), cfg$q, na.rm = TRUE),
                     .groups = "drop")
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Trajectory shape, NA-safe
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

classify <- function(early, net, thr_e, thr_l, tol = NULL) {
  if (is.null(tol)) tol <- mean(c(thr_e, thr_l)) / 2

  P <- cbind(`3m` = 0, `12m` = early, `18m` = net)   # relative positions
  P <- P - rowMeans(P)                                # centre, as in z-scoring

  L <- ifelse(P >  tol, "high",
       ifelse(P < -tol, "low", "middle"))

  out <- apply(L, 1, paste, collapse = "_")
  out[is.na(early) | is.na(net)] <- NA_character_
  out
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Main
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

age_changing <- function(obj, label, cfg = CFG) {
  message("\n=== ", label, " ===")
  feats <- detectable_genes(obj, cfg)
  if (length(feats) < 50)
    warning(label, ": only ", length(feats),
            " genes pass detection -- arm is likely underpowered")

  obs <- run_pairwise(obj, feats)
  thr <- calibrate(obj, feats, cfg)
  message("  permutation thresholds (|log2FC|):")
  print(as.data.frame(thr), row.names = FALSE)

  te <- thr$threshold[thr$comparison == "3m_to_12m"]
  tl <- thr$threshold[thr$comparison == "12m_to_18m"]
  tn <- thr$threshold[thr$comparison == "3m_to_18m"]

  wide <- obs %>%
    dplyr::select(gene, comparison, log2FC) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = comparison, values_from = log2FC) %>%
    dplyr::rename(early = `3m_to_12m`, late = `12m_to_18m`, net = `3m_to_18m`)

  pcts <- obs %>%
    dplyr::group_by(gene) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(max_abs_pct_diff = max(abs(pct_diff)), .groups = "drop")

  res <- wide %>%
    dplyr::left_join(pcts, by = "gene") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      max_abs_log2FC = pmax(abs(early), abs(late), abs(net)),
      passes = abs(early) > te | abs(late) > tl | abs(net) > tn,
      shape = classify(early, net, te, tn),
      sex    = label
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(passes) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(max_abs_log2FC))

  ## sanity report -- sparsity artefacts show up as absurd fold-changes
  med <- median(res$max_abs_log2FC)
  message(sprintf("  %d genes | median |log2FC| = %.2f | n NA shapes = %d",
                  nrow(res), med, sum(is.na(res$shape))))
  if (med > 2)
    warning(label, ": median |log2FC| = ", round(med, 2),
            " -- still sparsity-driven; raise CFG$min_cells")

  res
}
```


```{r}
male_genes   <- age_changing(neus_male,   "Male")
female_genes <- age_changing(neus_female, "Female")

write.csv(male_genes,   "mature_male_age_changing_genes.csv",   row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(female_genes, "mature_female_age_changing_genes.csv", row.names = FALSE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Cross-sex comparison
##
## Note the shared set is only interpretable if BOTH arms passed the sanity
## check above. A shared list built against a broken male arm is meaningless.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

shared <- dplyr::inner_join(male_genes, female_genes, by = "gene",
                            suffix = c("_M", "_F")) %>%
  dplyr::select(gene, shape_M, shape_F,
                early_M, late_M, net_M, early_F, late_F, net_F,
                max_abs_log2FC_M, max_abs_log2FC_F) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(same_shape = shape_M == shape_F)

write.csv(shared, "mature_comparison_age_changing_genes.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cat(sprintf("\nMale: %d | Female: %d | Shared: %d\n",
            nrow(male_genes), nrow(female_genes), nrow(shared)))
print(table(male_genes$shape,   useNA = "ifany"))
print(table(female_genes$shape, useNA = "ifany"))
```

```{r}
female_genes <- age_changing(immat_neus_female, "Female")

write.csv(male_genes,   "age_changing_male_v2.csv",   row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(female_genes, "age_changing_female_v2.csv", row.names = FALSE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. Cross-sex comparison
##
## Note the shared set is only interpretable if BOTH arms passed the sanity
## check above. A shared list built against a broken male arm is meaningless.
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

shared <- dplyr::inner_join(male_genes, female_genes, by = "gene",
                            suffix = c("_M", "_F")) %>%
  dplyr::select(gene, shape_M, shape_F,
                early_M, late_M, net_M, early_F, late_F, net_F,
                max_abs_log2FC_M, max_abs_log2FC_F) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(same_shape = shape_M == shape_F)

write.csv(shared, "age_changing_shared_v2.csv", row.names = FALSE)

cat(sprintf("\nMale: %d | Female: %d | Shared: %d\n",
            nrow(male_genes), nrow(female_genes), nrow(shared)))
print(table(male_genes$shape,   useNA = "ifany"))
print(table(female_genes$shape, useNA = "ifany"))
```

```{r}
CFG <- list(
  adt_min_median = 0,   # require median DSB-normalised signal > this,
                        # in EVERY age group -- placeholder, see note above
  n_perm = 20,
  q      = 0.95
)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Feature filter
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

adequate_adt <- function(obj, cfg = CFG) {
  dat  <- GetAssayData(obj, assay = "ADT", layer = "data")   # DSB-normalised
  ages <- as.character(obj$age)

  ok <- vapply(AGES, function(a) {
    idx <- ages == a
    apply(dat[, idx, drop = FALSE], 1, median) > cfg$adt_min_median
  }, logical(nrow(dat)))

  keep <- rownames(dat)[rowSums(ok) == length(AGES)]
  message(sprintf("  ADT filter: %d of %d antibodies retained",
                  length(keep), nrow(dat)))
  keep
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Pairwise comparisons (used for both real and permuted labels)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

run_pairwise <- function(obj, features, permute = FALSE, seed = 1) {
  ages <- as.character(obj$age)
  if (permute) { set.seed(seed); ages <- sample(ages) }
  obj$.age_use <- factor(ages, levels = AGES)
  Idents(obj) <- ".age_use"

  purrr::map_dfr(PAIRS, function(p) {
    FindMarkers(obj, ident.1 = p[1], ident.2 = p[2],
                assay = "ADT", features = features,
                logfc.threshold = 0, min.pct = 0,
                test.use = "wilcox", verbose = FALSE) %>%
      tibble::rownames_to_column("gene") %>%
      dplyr::transmute(gene,
                       comparison = paste0(p[2], "_to_", p[1]),
                       log2FC = avg_log2FC)
  })
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Permutation-calibrated thresholds
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

calibrate <- function(obj, features, cfg = CFG) {
  purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(cfg$n_perm),
                 ~ run_pairwise(obj, features, permute = TRUE, seed = .x)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(comparison) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(threshold = quantile(abs(log2FC), cfg$q, na.rm = TRUE),
                     .groups = "drop")
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Trajectory shape, NA-safe
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

classify <- function(early, net, thr_e, thr_l, tol = NULL) {
  if (is.null(tol)) tol <- mean(c(thr_e, thr_l)) / 2

  P <- cbind(`3m` = 0, `12m` = early, `18m` = net)   # relative positions
  P <- P - rowMeans(P)                                # centre, as in z-scoring

  L <- ifelse(P >  tol, "high",
       ifelse(P < -tol, "low", "middle"))

  out <- apply(L, 1, paste, collapse = "_")
  out[is.na(early) | is.na(net)] <- NA_character_
  out
}

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. Main
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

age_changing_adt <- function(obj, label, cfg = CFG) {
  message("\n=== ", label, " / ADT ===")
  feats <- adequate_adt(obj, cfg)
  if (length(feats) < 5)
    warning(label, ": only ", length(feats), " antibodies pass filter")

  obs <- run_pairwise(obj, feats)
  thr <- calibrate(obj, feats, cfg)
  message("  permutation thresholds (|log2FC|):")
  print(as.data.frame(thr), row.names = FALSE)

  te <- thr$threshold[thr$comparison == "3m_to_12m"]
  tl_step <- thr$threshold[thr$comparison == "12m_to_18m"]
  tn <- thr$threshold[thr$comparison == "3m_to_18m"]

  res <- obs %>%
    dplyr::select(gene, comparison, log2FC) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = comparison, values_from = log2FC) %>%
    dplyr::rename(early = `3m_to_12m`, late = `12m_to_18m`, net = `3m_to_18m`) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      max_abs_log2FC = pmax(abs(early), abs(late), abs(net)),
      passes = abs(early) > te | abs(late) > tl_step | abs(net) > tn,
      shape = classify(early, net, te, tn),
      sex    = label
    ) %>%
    dplyr::filter(passes) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(max_abs_log2FC))

  message(sprintf("  %d antibodies pass | median |log2FC| = %.2f",
                  nrow(res), median(res$max_abs_log2FC)))
  res
}

male_adt   <- age_changing_adt(neus_male,   "Male")
female_adt <- age_changing_adt(neus_female, "Female")

write.csv(male_adt,   "age_changing_male_adt.csv",   row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(female_adt, "age_changing_female_adt.csv", row.names = FALSE)

print(table(male_adt$shape,   useNA = "ifany"))
print(table(female_adt$shape, useNA = "ifany"))

shared <- dplyr::inner_join(male_adt, female_adt, by = "gene",
                            suffix = c("_M", "_F")) %>%
  dplyr::select(gene, shape_M, shape_F,
                early_M, late_M, net_M, early_F, late_F, net_F,
                max_abs_log2FC_M, max_abs_log2FC_F) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(same_shape = shape_M == shape_F)

write.csv(shared, "age_changing_shared_adt.csv", row.names = FALSE)

one_ab <- GetAssayData(neus_female, assay = "ADT", layer = "data")["Ms.Ly.6C", ]
hist(one_ab, breaks = 50)   # look for the valley between two modes
```
